observations:
Torah #278 is a very short, two-part teaching. The text contains exactly one use of bechina language, which is already captured in the dataset (edge 941, Package 1). A second proposed package was considered and rejected, as detailed below.

**Part 1 — חֲלִיף טוֹב and the Temple Vessels (Sentence 1):**
The first paragraph describes how through חֲלִיף טוֹב (a good exchange; possibly referencing a well-sharpened slaughter-knife) one can perceive the faces/aspects of the כֵּלִים שֶׁל בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ (Temple vessels). This is supported by Isaac's instruction to Esau ('שָׂא נָא כֵלֶיךָ') and interpreted via the Midrash (Bereshit Rabbah 65) as an allusion to the Temple vessels.

Critically, this paragraph uses exclusively allusion language — 'רָמַז' (hinted) and 'מְרַמֵּז' (alludes). It does NOT use bechina identity language ('X הוּא בְחִינַת Y', 'נִקְרָא', etc.). The Torah does not say that חֲלִיף טוֹב IS a bechina of the Temple vessels, or that the knife IS a bechina of anything — it says the knife REVEALS/SHOWS the vessels (a causal/instrumental relationship, i.e., eitza). The Midrash says כֵּלֶיךָ 'alludes to' (remez) the Temple vessels, not that it IS them by shared nature.

Test (framework §2): Does one produce the other, or are they both expressions of the same thing? Here, חֲלִיף טוֹב is an instrument that enables one to SEE the Temple vessels — it produces a perception, it does not share the same essential nature as the vessels. This is eitza, not bechina.

Conclusion for Part 1: No bechina-based package can be formed from the first paragraph. The concepts (חֲלִיף טוֹב, כֵּלִים שֶׁל בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, סַּכִּין הַיָּפָה) belong to the eitza layer of this Torah's teaching.

**Part 2 — Pinchas's Zealousness and the Tzaddik (Sentence 2):**
The second sentence has one explicit bechina ('בְּחִינַת') connecting the scriptural phrase about Pinchas to the quality of the Tzaddik who is jealous only for God. This single bechina forms Package 1, which is already in the dataset.

**New package threshold check:**
The threshold for proposing a new package is: 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain not covered by existing packages. Torah #278 has:
- 1 bechina instance (captured in Package 1)
- 0 additional bechina statements
- No concept cluster of 3+ nodes connected by bechina language

No new packages are proposed. The existing Package 1 represents the complete bechina structure of Torah #278.
